title: Your coding agent can direct a short film without a video model
summary: Your coding agent can make a short film with no video model: lemo-opuscar gives it 99 styles, and it renders frames, writes the score and narrates in code, in about 30 to 60 minutes per film: https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar
body_markdown:
lemo-opuscar has your coding agent make a short film with no video model at all. The agent writes the film as code: canvas and WebGL pages rendered frame by frame, an original score assembled from free sample libraries, and text-to-speech narration, all mixed by the agent. The project states it plainly: no video generation, no stock footage.

What you pick is a style. The library holds 99 of them in 15 categories, sorted by what the picture looks like, and each one comes with a short demo film made the same way and a `STYLE.md` the agent follows. The story comes from you.

## How a request becomes a film

The request is meant to fit on one line:

```text
Make a film in the Neon Tubes style about the coffee farm my family runs.
```

You can add a length, a narrator, your own photos or music. From there the agent asks once, up front, about anything it cannot decide about your topic, whether you have voice, music or other material of your own, and whether you want a storyboard first. Say yes to the storyboard and it stops one time to show the key shots in the real style. Otherwise it goes straight to the finished film.

Behind that sits a split I like. Three files divide the work:

- `DIRECTOR.md` covers story, sound, rhythm, camera, performance and self-checks.
- `TECHNIQUE.md` covers frame-by-frame rendering, voice, music and mixing.
- `styles/<style>/STYLE.md` describes how one style looks and sounds.

Because the story stays with you, the same style file can be reused across different films.

## What it costs to make one film

The project is upfront about the bill. A film takes an agent about 30 to 60 minutes and a fair amount of tokens. You need Node 20+, ffmpeg 7+ and Python 3.11+, or uv, and the agent installs the rest. Ubuntu 24.04 ships ffmpeg 6.1, which is too old, so the setup notes point you to a static build.

The project is also specific about models. It says it was built for Claude, that Fable, Opus and Sonnet all work with effort set to high, and that other models may not reproduce the styles well. Three styles (Manga Panels, Text Flash Cuts and Comic History Cartoon) need an image generator you bring, such as a Codex CLI account that can generate images. Without one, those three cannot start. Every other style works without it.

Default output is 1920x1080 at 24 fps, and some styles set their own frame rate.

## Turning a library style into your own

The newer feature is style editing. You can take a library style, say Ukiyo-e, and change it into a version that carries your brand colours, logo, fonts or recurring characters, or start from a blank page with a description like "a chalk-on-blackboard style, warm and slow". From a blank page, Claude picks the closest library style as the technique base and tells you why, and you agree or pick another.

Planning goes one question at a time: what the style is for, which platform (vertical feeds want 1080x1920 or 1080x1440), what to change, and a name. Before anything is touched, a library style is sorted into parts that are safe to change (palette, type, pace, sound, signature moves), parts that change its character (materials and rendering, colour logic, camera grammar) and its essence, which cannot change. The author describes this as the same process used to add new styles to the library. Your own styles live in `~/lemo-my-styles/` and survive updates and uninstalls.

## Where I would start

Install it as a Claude Code plugin:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar
claude plugin install lemo-opuscar@lemolab
```

Then run `/lemo-opuscar:lemo-opuscar` with nothing else and let it walk you through the choices. I would ask for the storyboard on the first film. One stop to check the key shots is cheap next to 30 to 60 minutes of agent time spent on a direction you did not want.
